a. What does the parent say about their responsibility in the poem “Whose Child is This”?
b. What is the poet’s suggestion about nature in the poem “Leisure”?
c. How does the poet feel about life without time for nature in the poem “Leisure”?
d. How does the parent show care for the child in the poem “Whose Child is This”?
e. Why is the childhood important according to the poem “Whose Child is This”?

g. What role does nature play in the poem “Leisure”?
h. What is the poet’s message in the poem “Leisure”?
stimulus_data:
ANSWER KEY — indicative content, 1 mark per answer. The poems are W. H. Davies’s “Leisure” and “Whose Child is This?”, in which a parent, a teacher and the community each claim the child in turn.
a. The parent claims the child as their own and accepts responsibility for loving, feeding, clothing and protecting the child.
b. The poet suggests we should stop and enjoy the beauty of nature instead of hurrying past it.
c. He calls such a life poor — a life full of care with no time to stand and stare is not worth living.
d. By feeding, clothing, nursing, loving and guiding the child day after day.
e. Because the care, love and teaching a child receives in childhood shape the person the child becomes.
f. The teacher claims the child too — as a learner to be taught, guided and helped to grow in knowledge and character.
g. Nature is the source of beauty and joy — boughs, sheep and cows, squirrels, streams full of stars, Beauty’s dance — that busy people never notice.
h. Life is impoverished if we are too busy with worldly cares to pause and appreciate the beauty around us.
